---
output:
  pdf_document:
    latex_engine: xelatex
header-includes:
- \usepackage{float}
- \usepackage{tabu}
- \usepackage{lipsum}
- \usepackage{fancyhdr}
---

<!--
Build-time guard: docker/Dockerfile renders THIS through the real
rmarkdown -> pandoc -> xelatex path (the report's actual toolchain), so the build
fails if the LaTeX environment can't produce a PDF.

It mirrors how RAAB7_reporter.Rmd loads LaTeX: the header-includes above are the
report's OWN explicit \usepackage set (float/tabu/lipsum/fancyhdr); everything
else (multirow, colortbl, ulem, booktabs, longtable, ...) is injected by kableExtra
below, and the rmarkdown template pulls the rest (e.g. lmodern). Do NOT list the
kableExtra-injected packages here too — that double-loads them and triggers a
LaTeX "option clash" (ulem). Keep header-includes in sync with the report preamble.

Prod has no network, so a missing package at render is unrecoverable; this catches
it at build (stale images once had multirow.sty / lmodern.sty missing).
-->

```{r tbl}
library(kableExtra)
kbl(head(mtcars, 3), booktabs = TRUE) |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position", "scale_down"))
```

```{r fig, fig.width=4, fig.height=3}
library(treemap)
treemap(data.frame(x = c("a", "b"), v = c(3, 1)),
        index = "x", vSize = "v", title = "guard")
```
